title: A sheaf of modules on a basis extends uniquely to a sheaf of modules
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space and $\mathcal B$ a set of open subsets of $X$ which is a basis of the topology, such that $U\cap V\in\mathcal B$ for $U,V\in\mathcal B$, and such that for every $U\in\mathcal B$ every covering of $U$ by members of $\mathcal B$ can be refined to a finite covering of $U$ by members of $\mathcal B$ (each member of the finite covering lies in some member of the given one). Let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of rings on $X$. Suppose given, for every $U\in\mathcal B$, an $\mathcal O(U)$-module $F(U)$, and for $V\subseteq U$ in $\mathcal B$ an additive map $r_{U,V}:F(U)\to F(V)$ with $r_{U,U}=\mathrm{id}$, $r_{V,W}r_{U,V}=r_{U,W}$ and $r_{U,V}(as)=a|_V\,r_{U,V}(s)$ for $a\in\mathcal O(U)$, such that for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and every finite covering $U=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ with $U_i\in\mathcal B$ and $n\ge0$ (for $n=0$, the empty covering of $U=\emptyset$, this says $F(\emptyset)=0$ when $\emptyset\in\mathcal B$) the sequence $0\to F(U)\to\prod_iF(U_i)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}F(U_i\cap U_j)$ is exact (an element is determined by its restrictions, and a family agreeing on the $U_i\cap U_j$ comes from an element). Then: (a) there is a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $F^{ext}$ on $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] together with $\mathcal O(U)$-linear isomorphisms $\iota_U:F^{ext}(U)\to F(U)$ for $U\in\mathcal B$ with $\iota_V(t|_V)=r_{U,V}(\iota_U(t))$; (b) for every sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal G$ on $X$ and every family of $\mathcal O(U)$-linear maps $\psi_U:F(U)\to\mathcal G(U)$, $U\in\mathcal B$, compatible with the restrictions, there is a unique morphism of $\mathcal O$-modules $\Psi:F^{ext}\to\mathcal G$ with $\Psi_U=\psi_U\circ\iota_U$ for all $U\in\mathcal B$, and $\Psi$ is an isomorphism if all $\psi_U$ are bijective; in particular $(F^{ext},\iota)$ is unique up to unique isomorphism; (c) for $x\in X$ the stalk $F^{ext}_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is the colimit of the $F(U)$ over the members $U\in\mathcal B$ containing $x$ (directed by reverse inclusion), via the maps $F(U)\xrightarrow{\iota_U^{-1}}F^{ext}(U)\to F^{ext}_x$.

source.place: Sheaves on Spaces, Section 009H (label section-bases): Definition 009J (sheaf on a basis), Lemma 009L (label lemma-cofinal-systems-coverings-standard-case: the sheaf condition on a cofinal system of coverings, here the finite ones), Lemma 009M (label lemma-condition-star-sections) and Lemma 009N (label lemma-extend-off-basis) with its proof (sections of the extension are compatible families of germs in the colimit stalks), Definition 009S, Lemma 009T (label lemma-extend-off-basis-module), Lemma 009U (label lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-modules)

proof.text: *Sheaf condition for all $\mathcal B$-coverings.* For $U\in\mathcal B$ let $C(U)$ be the set of finite $\mathcal B$-coverings $U=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_n$ ($n\ge0$). By the refinement hypothesis every $\mathcal B$-covering of $U$ (any family of members of $\mathcal B$ with union $U$) is refined by a member of $C(U)$, i.e. $C(U)$ is cofinal; note that the hypothesis is a finite refinement, not a finite subcovering, which is exactly what cofinality asks. The exactness hypothesis says that the underlying presheaf of sets of $F$ on $\mathcal B$ (with $s|_V=r_{U,V}(s)$; $U\cap V\in\mathcal B$ by hypothesis) satisfies the gluing condition (compatible on the $U_i\cap U_j$ implies unique amalgamation) for every member of $C(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-basis-sheaf-cofinal-coverings] it satisfies the gluing condition for every $\mathcal B$-covering $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ of every $U\in\mathcal B$, $I$ arbitrary.

source.place: Section 009H, Lemma 009L (label lemma-cofinal-systems-coverings-standard-case) and its proof via Lemma 009K

proof.text: *The extension as a sheaf of abelian groups.* By step 1, the presheaf of abelian groups $(F(U),r_{U,V})$ on $\mathcal B$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-on-basis-extends] ($\mathcal B$ is a basis closed under pairwise intersections). Hence there is a sheaf of abelian groups $F^{ext}$ on $X$ with group isomorphisms $\iota_U:F^{ext}(U)\to F(U)$, $U\in\mathcal B$, such that $\iota_V(t|_V)=r_{U,V}(\iota_U(t))$ for $V\subseteq U$ in $\mathcal B$.

source.place: Section 009H, Lemma 009N (label lemma-extend-off-basis) and Lemma 009Q (label lemma-extend-off-basis-structures)

proof.text: *The module structure (proof of (a)).* Following Stacks 009T, the multiplication is constructed on the level of presheaves of sets. Let $P$ be the presheaf of sets $W\mapsto\mathcal O(W)\times F^{ext}(W)$ on $X$ (componentwise restriction) and $Q$ the underlying sheaf of sets of $F^{ext}$ (a sheaf of abelian groups is a sheaf on underlying sets: the gluing condition is the same statement). For $U\in\mathcal B$ put $\mu_U(a,t)=\iota_U^{-1}(a\,\iota_U(t))$ for $a\in\mathcal O(U)$, $t\in F^{ext}(U)$. For $V\subseteq U$ in $\mathcal B$: $\iota_V(\mu_U(a,t)|_V)=r_{U,V}(a\,\iota_U(t))=a|_V\,r_{U,V}(\iota_U(t))=a|_V\,\iota_V(t|_V)=\iota_V(\mu_V(a|_V,t|_V))$, using the compatibility of $\iota$ (step 2) and the semilinearity of $r_{U,V}$; so $(\mu_U)_{U\in\mathcal B}$ is a family of maps $P(U)\to Q(U)$ compatible with the restrictions. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] (a) (values in sets) there is a unique morphism of presheaves of sets $\mu:P\to Q$ with these components on $\mathcal B$; write $a\cdot t=\mu_W(a,t)$ for every open $W$. Each module axiom is an equality of two morphisms of presheaves of sets into $Q$ built from $\mu$, the ring operations of $\mathcal O$ and the addition of $F^{ext}$ (all compatible with restrictions): $(ab)\cdot t=a\cdot(b\cdot t)$ and $(a+b)\cdot t=a\cdot t+b\cdot t$ as maps $\mathcal O\times\mathcal O\times F^{ext}\to F^{ext}$, $a\cdot(t+t')=a\cdot t+a\cdot t'$ as maps $\mathcal O\times F^{ext}\times F^{ext}\to F^{ext}$, $1\cdot t=t$ as maps $F^{ext}\to F^{ext}$. On every $U\in\mathcal B$ the two sides agree, because there $\mu_U$ is the $\mathcal O(U)$-module structure of $F(U)$ transported along the additive bijection $\iota_U$. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] (a) (two morphisms from a presheaf into a sheaf agreeing on $\mathcal B$ are equal) each axiom holds on every open $W$. So every $F^{ext}(W)$ is an $\mathcal O(W)$-module extending its group structure, the restrictions are semilinear (naturality of $\mu$), and $F^{ext}$ is a sheaf of abelian groups: it is a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Each $\iota_U$ is $\mathcal O(U)$-linear since $\iota_U(a\cdot t)=\iota_U(\mu_U(a,t))=a\,\iota_U(t)$, and compatible with restrictions by step 2. This is (a).

source.place: Section 009H, Definition 009S and Lemma 009T (label lemma-extend-off-basis-module: it suffices to construct the multiplication on the level of presheaves of sets), with the functoriality of Lemma 009O/009U for extending it

proof.text: *Morphisms out of $F^{ext}$ (proof of (b)).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules and $\psi_U:F(U)\to\mathcal G(U)$, $U\in\mathcal B$, $\mathcal O(U)$-linear and compatible with restrictions. The maps $\psi_U\circ\iota_U:F^{ext}(U)\to\mathcal G(U)$ are additive and compatible with restrictions (step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] (a) (values in abelian groups) there is exactly one morphism of sheaves of abelian groups $\Psi:F^{ext}\to\mathcal G$ with $\Psi_U=\psi_U\circ\iota_U$ for $U\in\mathcal B$. It is $\mathcal O$-linear: the two morphisms of presheaves of sets $\mathcal O\times F^{ext}\to\mathcal G$, $(a,t)\mapsto\Psi(a\cdot t)$ and $(a,t)\mapsto a\,\Psi(t)$, agree on every $U\in\mathcal B$ ($\iota_U$ and $\psi_U$ are $\mathcal O(U)$-linear), hence are equal by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] (a) (values in sets). Uniqueness of $\Psi$ among morphisms of $\mathcal O$-modules follows from uniqueness among morphisms of abelian sheaves. If every $\psi_U$ is bijective, every $\Psi_U$, $U\in\mathcal B$, is an isomorphism, so $\Psi$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of abelian groups by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] (b); its inverse is $\mathcal O$-linear on every open (the inverse of a bijective linear map is linear), so $\Psi$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Finally, if $(F',\iota')$ is another sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules with $\mathcal O(U)$-linear isomorphisms $\iota'_U:F'(U)\to F(U)$ compatible with restrictions, applying this to $\mathcal G=F'$, $\psi_U=\iota_U'^{-1}$ gives an isomorphism $\Psi:F^{ext}\to F'$ with $\iota'_U\Psi_U=\iota_U$, and it is the only morphism with this property; so $(F^{ext},\iota)$ is unique up to unique isomorphism. This is (b).

source.place: Section 009H, Lemma 009U (label lemma-restrict-basis-equivalence-modules: restriction to B is an equivalence, i.e. fully faithful, with inverse given by Lemma 009T) and Lemma 009O

proof.text: *Stalks (proof of (c)).* Let $x\in X$. The set $\mathcal B_x=\{U\in\mathcal B:x\in U\}$ is directed by reverse inclusion ($U\cap V\in\mathcal B_x$ for $U,V\in\mathcal B_x$). Let $F^{ext}_x$ be the stalk with germs $t\mapsto t_x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and put $\lambda_U=(\,\cdot\,)_x\circ\iota_U^{-1}:F(U)\to F^{ext}_x$ for $U\in\mathcal B_x$. These are compatible: for $V\subseteq U$ in $\mathcal B_x$ and $s\in F(U)$, $\iota_V^{-1}(r_{U,V}(s))=(\iota_U^{-1}s)|_V$ (step 2), and a section and its restriction have the same germ. We show that $(F^{ext}_x,(\lambda_U))$ is a colimit of the $F(U)$, $U\in\mathcal B_x$. Let $A$ be an abelian group and $\varphi_U:F(U)\to A$ additive maps with $\varphi_V\circ r_{U,V}=\varphi_U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-germs-on-basis] (i) every element of $F^{ext}_x$ is $t_x$ with $t\in F^{ext}(U)$, $U\in\mathcal B_x$; set $\varphi(t_x)=\varphi_U(\iota_U(t))$. This is well defined: if $t_x=t'_x$ with $t\in F^{ext}(U)$, $t'\in F^{ext}(U')$, by [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-germs-on-basis] (ii) there is $W\in\mathcal B_x$, $W\subseteq U\cap U'$, with $t|_W=t'|_W$, whence $\varphi_U(\iota_Ut)=\varphi_W(r_{U,W}\iota_Ut)=\varphi_W(\iota_W(t|_W))=\varphi_W(\iota_W(t'|_W))=\varphi_{U'}(\iota_{U'}t')$. It is additive (two germs are germs over a common $W\in\mathcal B_x$, by restriction), satisfies $\varphi\circ\lambda_U=\varphi_U$, and is the only such map since the images of the $\lambda_U$ cover $F^{ext}_x$. So $F^{ext}_x=\varinjlim_{U\in\mathcal B_x}F(U)$ via the $\lambda_U$. Moreover $\lambda_U(as)=a_x\lambda_U(s)$ for $a\in\mathcal O(U)$ ($\iota_U$ is linear and germs are multiplicative, [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]), so the identification is compatible with the $\mathcal O_x$-module structure. This is (c).

Five steps: (1) finite-covering sheaf condition implies gluing for all B-coverings by the cofinal-coverings lemma (new node lem-weil-pbc-basis-sheaf-cofinal-coverings, Stacks 009L/009K; the hypothesis is a finite refinement, which is cofinality); (2) extension as a sheaf of abelian groups (new node lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-on-basis-extends, Stacks 009M/009N/009Q; Mathlib's comparison lemma sheafInducedTopologyEquivOfIsCoverDense with coverDense_inducedFunctor gives it once the gluing condition is shown to be the induced-topology sheaf condition, recorded in its searches); (3) the O-module structure, constructed on presheaves of sets as Stacks 009T says, by extending the action O x F^ext -> F^ext from B and checking the module axioms on B, both with the reviewed Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis (restrictHomEquivHom/hom_ext); (4) clause (b) from the same leaf (restrictHomEquivHom, hom_ext, isIso_iff_isIso_basis) plus linearity on B; (5) clause (c) by the universal property, from the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-stalk-germs-on-basis (exists_mem_germ_eq_of_isBasis, germ_eq_of_isBasis, Stalks.lean:484/491).
